To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the administration of bovine or ovvine insulin intravenously to young NOD mice downregulates several autoimmune parameters associated insulin-dependent diabetes.
soluble bovine and ovine insulin given shortly after weaning to female NOD mouse offspring have a downregulating influence on spontaneous and induced autoimmunity to insulin.
the protective effect afforded by soluble insulin given intravenous to NOD mice is independent of the species origin of the insulin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an effective treatment for insulin-dependent diabetes.
the development of a vaccine to prevent or cure insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus (IDDM), and we have been investigating the use of soluble insulin as a tolerogen.
the development of an immunomodulating agent for the prevention of insulin-dependent diabetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the protective effect of bovine insulin in NOD mice is not dependent on the sheep-specific T-cell epitope.
bovine insulin is a more effective immunomodulator than ovine insulin in the NOD mouse model.
the protective effects of both bovine and ovine insulin were mediated by a common epitope, which is shared by both insulins and is located on the A-chain of insulin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
both bovine and ovine insuins can modulate spontaneous autoimmune diabetes, and that the protective mechanism is not sheep-specific.
the immunogenicity of insulin is not necessarily related to the effectiveness of insulin in protecting against spontaneous autoimmune diabetes.
the NOD mouse has an inherent defect in its immune system which allows it to mount a spontaneous autoimmune response to insulin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a heterologous insulin to modulate autoimmunity in NOD mice may be more effective and more practical than the use of homologous insulin.
it is possible to modulate spontaneous autoimmunity in young NOD mice by intravenously administering insulin.
intravenous insulin administration is an effective method of preventing diabetes in NOD mice.
